quest.title: The Quest for a Cure
quest.description: There seems to be something else going on with the poison in Jialiang's body...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x27825, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Go to the west of Qingce Village

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, there's a house all the way out here? It's so well hidden, Paimon's never noticed it before...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Nor have I... and I've hosted clinics at Qingce Village many times in the past. If you ask me... Jiangli was trying to remain unnoticed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that reminds Paimon. We meant to ask earlier, but it slipped our minds in the rush to get here... Could you tell us more about Jiangli? You said she was your fellow disciple, right?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: She was indeed. We studied medicine together under the same master near Chenyu Vale.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: She is several years older than I and also began her travels far earlier than me. As a result, the time I spent studying alongside her was rather short.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Supposedly, she met an herb gatherer sometime during her travels and decided to settle down with him. That must have been Jialiang.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Changsheng, are you saying... Neither of you had actually met Jialiang or Ayu before all of this?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...Jiangli did occasionally come back to Chenyu Vale to see our master, but for whatever reason, she hardly ever talked about her family.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: The last time she visited us, she and master had some sort of a quarrel... We never heard from her after that. It almost seemed as if she'd gone into hiding.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Quarrel? What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: I don't know. I did not witness the argument myself.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Nor did Master ever explain it to me. All he would say is that, should I ever encounter Jiangli or her family in the future... I should do everything in my power to help them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So that's why you went to such extreme lengths to help Jialiang.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: No. Even if my master had never said anything, it would still be my duty as a doctor to help him. My decision would have remained the same.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon never knew you were so selfless, Baizhu. Paimon always had you down as the sneaky scheming type... Sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Heh, so a few words from me is enough to dispel all your suspicions, hmm? You ought not be quite so quick to relax your guard, Paimon... Sometimes, even the "good guys" have their own private agenda.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the... Okay, that was the most suspicious-sounding thing you've ever said!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Let's leave the idle chatter there for now. Jiangli has lived in this house for many years — there must be something here that can shed a little light on this whole situation.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Let's split up, but if anyone finds anything, we'll examine it together.

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Observe Wooden Pillar
dialogues.text: (Several faint marks can be seen on the pillar. Maybe it was used to record Ayu's height as he grew up.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Wooden Pillar
dialogues.text: (There's some faded writing near the bottom mark: "The more quickly Ayu grows up, the sooner... can leave...")

dialogues.speaker: Observe Wooden Pillar
dialogues.text: (...Judging by the number of marks on the pillar, the family has led a secluded existence here for many, many years.)

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Observe Stack of Wood
dialogues.text: (The firewood is neatly stacked, and the logs were cut with great power and precision. Whoever chopped the firewood must have been physically fit.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Stack of Wood
dialogues.text: (...Some logs at the bottom of the pile have begun to rot. It must have been a while since any new wood was added to the pile.)

talks.objective: Look for clues in the area

dialogues.speaker: Diary With Childish Handwriting
dialogues.text: "...Some roof tiles broke. Mom and I tried to get up and take a look, but we didn't manage. Luckily, dad was able to fix them in no time!"

dialogues.speaker: Diary With Childish Handwriting
dialogues.text: "...The dinner table was a bit wobbly today when we sat down to eat... Dad tried to fix it, but ended up breaking one of the legs by accident..."

dialogues.speaker: Diary With Childish Handwriting
dialogues.text: "...Dad's forgetting things again. I'll have to write it all down for now, and read it back to him when he's feeling a bit better..."

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: You called?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Waaah!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Ugh, gets Paimon every time!

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: ...Are all adepti in the habit of materializing out of thin air like this?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...Well, this is unexpected.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...Huh? It's you?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Baizhu, of Bubu Pharmacy. I do believe I've had the pleasure before.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...The Lantern Rite when we met briefly, I was unaware of your true identity. I... must apologize for the discourtesy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You two already know each other?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Our paths have crossed once before.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...I sense the presence of evil spirits. Is this why you called me?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Xiao everything that has happened...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: So someone has been concocting demonic poison...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Too often, fervent desires drive mortals to abandon all regard for their own safety... It is lamentable.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: I now know what you seek. It is true that a god's remains are buried beneath the foundations of Qingce Village.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: A vile monster known as the Chi once wrought havoc over this land, before it was subdued by Rex Lapis...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: The land was finally cleansed of poison when Rex Lapis used statues in his likeness to seal the serpent's remains. Qingce Village was founded sometime after that.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: The seal is still mostly intact. If the Chi is the source, then it must be some of its blood leaking from deep underground.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: However... its aura is faint and barely detectable. You will need to investigate further to identify the location of the leak.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I see.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: I do not like to intervene against mortals unless absolutely necessary.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: But when demonic forces are involved, things can spiral out of control... If that happens, be sure to call my name again.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: ...Hmm?

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...Nothing.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: I do not wish to sway decisions that are mortals' to make, but...

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: ...Immortality may not be the blessing that you imagine it to be.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...I shall treasure your words of instruction, Master Adeptus.

response.speaker: Xiao
response.text: Farewell.

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: What a strange adeptus... Rather different from the way I remember them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's Xiao for ya! And thanks to him, we've finally got some concrete info to go off of.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: If the god remains are leaking from underground, Jiangli must be paying a visit to a subterranean cave on her "herb gathering" trips. If we can find the cave...

response.speaker: Herbalist Gui
response.text: Mas... Master! *panting* Master — there's a problem!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gui? ...Did you run all the way from Bubu Pharmacy?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: What happened? Don't panic, just catch your breath, and tell me everything.

response.speaker: Herbalist Gui
response.text: It's... It's Jialiang...

response.speaker: Herbalist Gui
response.text: He was... he was fine one minute, and then... he suddenly took a turn for the worse!

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Already? How?

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Based on past experience, he should have been fine for the next three days at least...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...It seems that my worst fears have been confirmed.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Everyone, back to Bubu Pharmacy, now!

choices.text: Actually, I wanted to ask you about dead gods...

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Dad! What's wrong? Dad...

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Ugh... Urghhh...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Don't be scared, Dr. Baizhu will be back soon...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: How is he doing?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Dr. Baizhu, you're back! My dad was doing fine earlier, but then he suddenly started coughing up blood! Now, he can't even get a full word out anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: When Gui left, he was still conscious. But now...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...Gui, please take Jialiang to the back room and prepare for treatment.

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Yes, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Ayu. I will cure your father.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: How time flies... Jiangli's had a son, and he's all grown up...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I wonder if Jiangli's changed at all, after all these years?

talks.objective: Talk to Ayu and the others

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: How are you feeling, Dad? Are you still hurting anywhere? You're not gonna suddenly collapse again, are you...?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Much better, Ayu, I'm feeling much better. In fact... I can't explain it, but somehow I feel even better than usual.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Hmm? Wait... Where's Dr. Baizhu? I still haven't had a chance to thank him... Seems he moved me here before I came to.

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Master said he needed to take a quick rest, and asked me to bring you out of the treatment room... He hasn't emerged yet, so he must still be resting.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Oh, really? ...Well, he must be tired from treating me for two nights in a row.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: *sigh* I don't know how I can begin to repay him for saving my life. I'll have to discuss it properly with Jiangli once we find her...

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Hmm... Speaking of which, has there been any word of her whereabouts yet?

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: No, the Adventurers' Guild hasn't gotten back to me yet. I'll go check with them again in a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: I'll come with— Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Don't forget what Master said — you're still not out of the woods yet, Jialiang. I strongly suggest that you stay and rest at Bubu Pharmacy for now. I can accompany Ayu to the Adventurers' Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* I suppose you're right... I'll have to rely on you this time.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: Though, on the bright side, this means I can thank Dr. Baizhu in person once he's finished resting...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Baizhu hasn't shown his face ever since he went in to treat Jialiang again. Do you think he...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Let's go check up on him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Hey, wait up!

talks.objective: Wait for Baizhu outside the back room

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: ...You're finally awake? Phew. That was far too risky, even with me here to help you balance your qi.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...There was no time, I had no other choice. In any case, it was not completely without benefit to myself — I managed to learn something.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Jiangli's design is quite brilliant. She makes numerous innovations that I can learn from... Alas, if only there wasn't a catch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So, how much longer do you think Baizhu's gonna nap for?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: They've been outside waiting for you the whole time while you were asleep. Shall we at least go and show our faces?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Surely he hasn't... There's no way he could've just—

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Who's talking behind our backs again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Baizhu! Changsheng!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you both okay?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Of course, there's no need to be concerned. I merely had to transfer a rather large amount of life force on this occasion. But with Changsheng's help, I will recover in time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jialiang seemed fine yesterday. Why did he need more life-saving treatment again so soon?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I made an error in my initial diagnosis. Jialiang is in fact suffering from more than one ailment.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...And as a result, his life force depleted at a greater rate than I had anticipated.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? You mean, even if you got all the poison out of him... he'd still be sick?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Yes... but more pertinently, the poison in Jialiang's system is there precisely because it is being used to manage his underlying medical condition.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Jialiang has a rare congenital heart condition, and ongoing treatment is essential to maintaining healthy functioning of his heart meridian. Left untreated, it puts the patient at risk of coughing up blood and fainting, and in the longer term, causes irreversible damage to the internal organs.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Though it was created from god remains, this formula is not a poison in Jialiang's case. Rather, it's his medication.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Had he not taken it all these years, he likely would have died a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So that's why Jiangli did it...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Still, using poison to treat a disease is hardly a viable long-term solution. As time passed, and the poison accumulated in his system, it began to impact his cognition.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Moreover, the longer he relied upon this medicine, the more resistant his body became to it. Jiangli had to concoct ever greater quantities to ensure its continued efficacy, or he could have still perished at any moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That explains why Ayu said his dad has been getting worse... and why his mom went off to "gather herbs"...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: God remains are extremely dangerous to be around, because humans have no natural defense against them. I shudder to think how many times Jiangli has exposed herself to them...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: I fear that the situation is just as that adeptus described... In an effort to save Jialiang's life, Jiangli has abandoned all regard for her own safety.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: I never suspected that even Jiangli would turn to the same path as so many others over the years... Perhaps this is the inevitable course of fate...

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: To sacrifice one's own life to save others... To go beyond human means in order to do the impossible, whatever the cost may be...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Fate"...?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...Well, I think that it's too early to say with any certainty what fate has in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: In any case, I have stabilized Jialiang's condition for now, so our immediate priority should be to get ourselves back to Qingce Village and find out where Jiangli is.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Her regular exposure to god remains over such a long period will have been catastrophic for her health.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: And given that she's already been missing for several days... I am fearing the worst.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...I—It's me, Traveler, Dr. Baizhu.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, it's Jialiang! ...Don't tell Paimon you overheard everything already...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: Dr. Baizhu... Please let me come with you!

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: You have already done so much for my family. I can no longer just sit here and watch while you put yourself at risk for Jiangli's sake.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: After all, if it wasn't for me, she wouldn't have had to put herself in harm's way in the first place... I know I won't be of much help in battle, but at the very least, I can show you the way.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: ...I'm sure I'll be able to remember, I know there's a spot where she says goodbye to me every time she goes to "gather her herbs." I'm sure I'll remember... I—I have to remember! Ugh... *cough*

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Be careful! If you get too agitated, your blood pressure and stress levels will rise, putting further pressure on your heart... For your own safety, you should stay here and rest.

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: No! We're out of time! We have to go now... right now...

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: Before I forget everything again...!

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...This trip will be extremely dangerous, and there is a very real possibility that you will not return from it... Are you sure you're prepared for that?

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: Hah... I never expected to live this long in the first place. My death is already long overdue... So why should I fear it?

response.speaker: Jialiang
response.text: There's only one thing I fear now... and that's that I'll forget her again before we manage to find her...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: ...Very well. Then, follow me.

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Dr. Baizhu, are you heading out again?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Yes... This could be a long one... Could you please prepare a dose of the usual formula?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Please add an extra measure of Mist Grass Pollen, and one dose each of the ingredients from the third and fifth compartments of my medicine cabinet... I hope it works.

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Dr. Baizhu... Do you mean...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Hop to it, now. And remember to be careful with the cauldron this time... You don't want to burn yourself again.

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: ...Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What is this?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Changsheng and I found a hidden compartment... This is what was hidden inside.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...God remains?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Ah, you sense it too? You're right — this is a poison concocted using god remains.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Is it... breathing? Paimon's not seeing things, is she?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: No, your eyes do not deceive you. I do believe the poison in this bottle is... alive.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Alive"?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Some toxins act a lot like living organisms... I read about this once in "The Origins and Symptoms of Diseases." This ancient class of poisons consists of "mother" and "minor" lodes, capable of sustaining a connection over vast distances.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: If it's a concoction of this kind we're dealing with, then both the poison in Jialiang's system and this one here are likely minor lodes... offshoots, essentially.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Offshoots? So... the main body is somewhere else?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Correct. Whoever is administering the poison can manipulate the source to indirectly control the poisoned individual's behavior and even cognition. Similarly, the poisoned individual will hear, to a varying extent, the call of the source.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The call of the... Wait! So back when Jialiang ran off, maybe that explains where he was heading!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...He was going back towards Qingce Village!

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Only one thing could've been drawing him there. The source of the god remains used as the poison's key ingredient... the mother lode.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is getting crazier and crazier! What kind of person would do all this just to poison Jialiang?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... Why's everyone gone quiet all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: ...Since this poison was carefully hidden away in a secret compartment, the one who concocted it is likely a resident of the house.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean, Jialiang? Why would he poison himself?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Think a little harder, Paimon. Someone else who lives here... and who might have expertise in crafting drugs...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So you're saying... *gasp* It was Jiangli!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but that doesn't make any sense either! Why would she poison her own husband?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...I agree, it makes little sense. Jiangli does not strike me as the kind of person who would do such a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Look at the facts, though. How many people in the entirety of Liyue have the ability to concoct a poison from god remains?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: ...It's too early to draw any conclusions. We should question Jialiang about it once he has made more progress in his recovery.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you know of a method to neutralize the poison?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Yes. According to "The Origins and Symptoms of Diseases," the minor lodes will disappear if the mother lode is purged...

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: So, if we can find and destroy the source of these god remains, the poison will leave Jialiang's system without the need for any further treatment.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Do you know anything about god remains in Qingce Village?

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: *sigh* Even the history books have no record of this. The only ones who'll know anything are those old fogeys who've been hanging around here since the beginning of time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? Didn't you use to be on good terms with the adepti, though? You sure they didn't tell you anything about this?

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Well, uh... Ahem...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Changsheng's memories and powers are not what they were in her prime.

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: These days, she has to enter a contract with a mortal and share their life force just to sustain her own life. I fear that such ancient events are long gone from her memory by now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Whoa, what? Enter a contract? Share life force? Sounds like some pretty spooky sorcery if you ask Paimon...

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Hey! Plenty of people would jump at the chance to join forces with a powerful being like me!

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: With my assistance in rebalancing your qi, not only can you extend your lifespan, but you will also be stronger, healthier, and able to eat whatever you like with no risk of upsetting your stomach!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stronger and healthier? Wow, that's amazing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Baizhu, maybe when you retire, you can let Paimon sign a contract with Changsheng for a few days, hee-hee...

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Unfortunately, Changsheng's contract has strict requirements regarding the host's temperament. None of her hosts have ever been exempted from these rules. I fear that I will be unable to accommodate your wishes, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Temperament? Hey, what are you trying to say? Did you just subtly insult Paimon to her face?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Strange, Baizhu has a weak constitution...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And didn't his master pass away at an early age?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ughhhh... Paimon's mad! You're getting ugly nicknames, both of you! Baizhu, you're Mannequin Man! Changsheng, you're just... a Pain in the Neck!

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: This is exactly why your natural temperament makes you woefully unsuited to being my host!

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: Alright, everybody, calm down. Back to the matter at hand. Is there any way at all for us to seek counsel from the adepti about this?

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: Hmph, with how antisocial they are? If it were up to them, they'd go their whole lives without showing their faces to the common folk...

response.speaker: Changsheng
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Baizhu
response.text: #Seems you're as well-connected as they say, {NICKNAME}. We are truly fortunate to have you on our side.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... If you're talking about who Paimon thinks you're talking about... you'd better do the honors.

choices.text: I do have someone that I can call.

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Are you heading out now, Dr. Baizhu?

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Yes. While I'm gone, I leave Bubu Pharmacy in your and Qiqi's capable hands.

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Rest assured, the moment anything comes up that you should know about, I'll inform you immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Phew... she's finally gone. She's gone for good now, right? ...Right?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Huh... Fancy running into you guys at a place like this. What are the chances!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Uh, nothing? I was just battling against some writer's block, so I took a stroll to see if I could get my muse back... Mm... mm, yep, i—it's working... "Stealthy as a snake, she can hear them coming, plants a little bait, and they all come running"...

choices.text: Won't your continued absence affect Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's business?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: It's fine, I have someone taking care of the books while I'm gone... Hold up, now that you mention it, I probably shouldn't stick around here too long...

choices.text: Still worried about what Baizhu's up to?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: ...You'd better not snitch on me, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: *sigh* Your mother's been missing for days now, but here I am, sitting here and doing nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: Don't think about that, Dad! Just concentrate on getting better. ...It's been years since we were last able to talk to each other like this.

dialogues.speaker: Jialiang
dialogues.text: So it has... In the blink of an eye, you're already so grown up...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Please don't worry. Dr. Baizhu, will find a way...

dialogues.speaker: Ayu
dialogues.text: But, but... *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Herbalist Gui
dialogues.text: Dr. Baizhu is still treating the patient. Please do not disturb him for now.

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Paimon! Come quick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Baizhu's not gonna use Changsheng's secret art again, is he...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there really no other way to save Jialiang?
